title: Credit-pool fanout and soft-demotion routing for tiered access
creator: Marcus Liu
description: Implement a credit-aware admission controller that routes traffic across free/paid/enterprise lanes with soft-demotion behavior and region-aware model variant fallbacks. Goals: 1) keep enterprise customers within SLA under pressure, 2) allow paid plans graceful degradation (soft-demote to slower variants or regional spill), 3) provide predictable best-effort experience for free tier while protecting paid capacity. Must integrate with existing quota ledger, plan-credit pools, and region affinity metadata. Deliverables: design doc, simulator, admission-controller implementation, e2e test harness, pilot release to a subset of tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-plan soft-reserve percentage configurable per cycle
When a plan exhausts soft-reserve, requests are demoted to lower-priority lane or queued with backoff instead of hard-reject
Regional fallback chooses compatible model variant with equivalent API (same output schema) and documented quality delta
Observed P95 latency for enterprise routes remains within configured SLA for 99% of pilot traffic
End-to-end tests that simulate quota spikes and cross-region outages pass in CI
notes: This approach uses a two-tier credit model: (1) hard-allocated reserved credits for enterprise plans, and (2) soft-reserve buckets per plan tier that can be temporarily borrowed with increasing demotion probability. Demotion paths include: regional model variant fallback (same schema, quantized/shorter context), latency-tolerant queued execution, and degraded output confidence flag to the caller. We must document quality deltas and provide telemetry to product and customer success.
tradeoffs: Strong prioritization protects high-value customers but risks poor UX for free users during sustained overload. Soft-demote keeps requests alive but increases tail latency and complexity in billing attribution. Regional fallbacks reduce latency cost but may introduce model-answer drift; must be surfaced via .quality_delta and used in A/B evaluations.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature flags and simulator (canary in staging). 2) Small pilot: enable for 2 enterprise tenants and 20 paid tenants in us-west-2 with observability hooks. 3) Collect metrics for 72h: success rate, demotion rate, billing deltas, model-quality regression. 4) Iterate on thresholds and soft-reserve sizes. 5) Gradual ramp to 25% of traffic, then global with opt-out mechanism.
qa_notes: Simulator repo contains scenario scripts (burst patterns, cross-region outage, quota exhaustion). Add CI tests that assert no hard 429s for paid/enterprise during simulated transient spikes unless total hard-allocated capacity is exceeded. Load test with mkbench to verify demotion behavior at 2x expected peak.
open_questions: What is the default soft-reserve percentage per tier? (proposal: Enterprise 30%, Paid 10%, Free 2%)
How do we bill for requests that were served by downgraded model variants? (at full rate with credit refund vs. discounted charge)
Should we expose demotion_reason and fallback_variant in the standard API response headers?
